## core
- `core/area_port.gd`: What the Router needs from the area that is playing (a base class to override; the default does nothing)
- `core/asset_manifest.gd`: Checks assets/manifest.json: every file under the assets folder (except *.import, .gdignore, *.md and the manifest itself) has an entry with a non-empty source and licence
- `core/audio_director.gd`: All game audio (autoload AudioDirector)
- `core/battle_session.gd`: One battle from the Router's side: launches a BattleRunner beside the area, and when the stage ends turns its result into GameState changes
- `core/content_db.gd`: All authored game data (autoload ContentDB)
- `core/defs/def.gd`: Base of every content definition: an id, how it reads itself from JSON, and which other ids it needs
- `core/defs/def_reader.gd`: Typed, validated reads from one JSON object
- `core/defs/flow_rules_def.gd`: Numbers and ids of the game flow (content/prototype/flow.json): which arena battles use, the music of exploring and of fighting, how long the player must stand still for a spot to count as safe (the unstuck target), and where the debug labels sit
- `core/defs/transition_def.gd`: A screen transition between flow states: a plain fade or the qamariya-glass shatter, how long it runs and the colour it fades through (content/ui/transitions.json)
- `core/event_bus.gd`: Global signals between features (autoload EventBus)
- `core/game_state.gd`: Everything a save file holds (autoload GameState)
- `core/save/router_saves.gd`: Helper for Router save operations: slot checks and file I/O delegates
- `core/save/save_codec.gd`: Pure save format: migrate() lifts any old save dictionary to the current version one step at a time (_v1_to_v2, _v2_to_v3, _v3_to_v4), and sanitize() drops content ids the game no longer knows
- `core/save/save_service.gd`: Save slots on disk: <dir>/slot_N.json, written atomically (tmp file, then rename over the old one, with the previous save kept as slot_N.json.bak)
- `core/scene_router.gd`: Game flow owner (autoload Router): title -> area -> battle arena -> area, new game, save and load, unstuck, and the play-time clock
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/a.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/manifest.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/unlisted.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_ok/manifest.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_ok/sub/note.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_content/combatants.json`: content: combatant x1
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/bad.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/dup_a.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/dup_b.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/save_v3.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/test_asset_manifest.gd`: Asset manifest: every shipped asset has a source and licence; the checker catches missing entries, empty licences and entries without files (fixtures), and ignores notes, .import files and the manifest
- `core/tests/test_content_db.gd`: The shipped content loads with no problems, and the validator catches broken content
- `core/tests/test_def_reader.gd`: DefReader int lists and cross-key problems, and the encounter definition built on them
- `core/tests/test_game_state.gd`: Save data survives a round trip through JSON, a version-1 save migrates, and an unknown version is refused
- `core/tests/test_save_codec.gd`: SaveCodec: a v3 fixture migrates to v4, unknown versions are refused, unknown content ids are dropped with a warning, and the full v4 state (money, bag, vitals with hp 0, cleared patrols) round trips through GameState
- `core/tests/test_save_service.gd`: SaveService: round trip, summary, an existing slot is replaced (the rename overwrites on Windows too) with the old save kept as .bak, and corrupt files give a clear error
- `core/tests/test_text_db.gd`: Player text: every localization CSV loads, keys translate, and a malformed file is reported
- `core/text_db.gd`: Player text (autoload TextDB): loads every res://localization/*.csv (header "keys,<lang>,...") into the TranslationServer at startup, so tr("KEY") works

## features
- `features/art/defs/clip_def.gd`: The timing of one model clip (an animation of the shared library): its length, whether it loops, and for a one-shot the Hades-style retiming (docs/design/characters-3d.md 4): the clip runs slow to `windup_t`, holds a beat, runs fast through the strike to `strike_end_t` (`impact_t` lands inside it) and eases out
- `features/art/defs/model_def.gd`: One live 3D character model (docs/design/characters-3d.md 5): a skinned glTF (or a rigid model built in code) with its height, footprint, anchors (bone names), the facade state -> ClipDef map, stride and turn speed, skin tint, and the parts it wears
- `features/art/defs/model_part_def.gd`: One part worn by a model on a bone (a "part" of a ModelDef): hair or brows from a glTF, a rigid mesh from a glb (the drone's hull), a garment lathed around the bone's up axis from a radius profile (skirt, coat, head wrap), a sleeve (capsule from the bone to its child), or the grandfather's jambiyah hilt (Rodin grip and sheath scenes)
- `features/art/defs/palette_def.gd`: The locked colour palette: one letter per colour ("." is transparent and never listed here)
- `features/art/defs/sprite_def.gd`: One pixel sprite: rows of palette letters ('.' = transparent), all the same width, feet on the last row
- `features/art/defs/visual_rules_def.gd`: Numbers for how a CharacterVisual looks and moves: art scale, idle breathing, walking (bob, squash and stretch, lean, dust), turning, the blob shadow, and the battle motions (anticipation, lunge with afterimages, recoil, hurt, knocked out, revive, victory hop)
- `features/art/logic/clip_timing.gd`: Pure retiming of a one-shot clip (ClipDef): real seconds <-> clip seconds
- `features/art/logic/locomotion.gd`: Pure walking maths for a model: which gait a ground speed means, the playback rate that keeps feet from sliding (speed / stride), a smoothed speed, the lean into acceleration and the foot contacts a gait loop passes
- `features/art/logic/model_gait.gd`: Pure choice of a model's looping clip: which gait (idle, walk, run) its measured ground speed and the state the facade asked for mean, and the playback rate that keeps its feet on the ground
- `features/art/logic/pixel_art.gd`: Turns a palette-indexed sprite (rows of letters) into an Image or texture
- `features/art/logic/pose_match.gd`: Pure maths of pose retargeting between two humanoid rigs with the same bone names but other bone axes and rest poses (a Rodin body driven by the Quaternius library): a constant per-bone offset so the target bone always points where the source bone points, and the hips' travel scaled from one leg length to the other
- `features/art/logic/yaw_turn.gd`: Pure turning for a model: the yaw (radians, about +y; 0 faces +z) of a ground direction and a capped step toward it that always takes the short way round
- `features/art/tests/test_character_motion.gd`: CharacterVisual motion: the shader material carries the data (minimum light, rim), knocked out / revived snap to the right look, the battle motions and the little effects (dust, afterimages, shadow) run without errors, and the sprite stays crisp (nearest filtering)
- `features/art/tests/test_model_defs.gd`: The data behind live 3D characters (content/art/models.json, clips.json) against the imported assets: every model maps all nine states to clips that exist, every clip names a real animation of the shared library with its length and an impact inside it, the bodies keep the rig's bone names, every anchor and part bone resolves, and the budgets hold (bones, triangles, surfaces, textures)
- `features/art/tests/test_model_logic.gd`: The pure maths behind live 3D characters: ClipTiming (wind-up, hold, strike, recovery and the events on that curve), Locomotion (gait, stride to playback rate, lean, foot contacts passed) and YawTurn (the capped short-way turn)
- `features/art/tests/test_model_source.gd`: The live 3D source behind the CharacterVisual facade: the model is built and painted, clips announce impact and end on the retimed curve (and wait for the hit pause), the body turns by yaw and never by a negative scale, the feet pace the ground and sound a footstep on each foot contact, a knocked-out body stays down, the grandfather's hilt is drawn for a strike and sheathed after, and a CharacterVisual without a model def falls back to the pixel sprite
- `features/art/tests/test_pose_match.gd`: Retargeting (PoseMatch, PoseFollow): the swing turns one direction into another, the per-bone offset makes the target bone point where the source bone points (at rest and after a turn), the hips travel scales with hip height, and a pose_source model's body follows its hidden source (Zayd's Rodin model stands up with the hand below the head); mirrored, the other arm does the move (Zayd's cast raises his prosthetic right arm)
- `features/art/tests/test_rodin_parts.gd`: Feras's Rodin pieces after tools/rodin: Zayd's baked dagger is pressed flat onto his chest (the code hilt is his only jambiyah), the grandfather's hilt is the Rodin grip above the belt origin and the Rodin sheath below it curving forward (the blade stays the code one), and the survey drone's hull is the Rodin mesh at hover height
- `features/art/tests/test_sprites.gd`: Prototype T7: every sprite is well formed and uses only palette letters; PixelArt and CharacterVisual work
- `features/art/tests/test_visual_contract.gd`: The CharacterVisual contract: play(state, facing), the anchors, clip events, the pixel and puppet sources behind the facade, and the pulse flag that switches the whole-body squash off for puppets
- `features/art/view/character.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_fx.gd`: The small effects around one CharacterVisual: a soft blob shadow on the floor, dust puffs at the feet and the fading afterimages of a lunge
- `features/art/view/character_ghost.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_hull.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_motion.gd`: The root moves of a CharacterVisual: they slide `root` and nothing else (the picture and its squash belong to the VisualSource)
- `features/art/view/character_skin.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_visual.gd`: A character standing in the 3D world (feet on the node's origin): the facade the game talks to
- `features/art/view/garment_mesh.gd`: Stand-in clothing built in code from a ModelPartDef (until Feras's own models): a lathe (a skirt, a coat, a head wrap) turned from a radius profile, and `prim`, which adds a coloured primitive to a SurfaceTool so a whole prop (the jambiyah) is one mesh with vertex colours (the skin shader multiplies COLOR into the albedo)
- `features/art/view/hilt_mesh.gd`: The stand-in for Zayd's grandfather's jambiyah (Heirloom `grandfather_hilt`), built in code from the part's colours until Feras's picture becomes a model: a curved horn grip with two silver bands, a T pommel with a carnelian stone, a curved blade, and a curved leather sheath with silver throat and tip
- `features/art/view/hilt_parts.gd`: The grandfather's jambiyah as nodes (the part's Rodin grip and sheath scenes, else HiltMesh's stand-in; the blade is always HiltMesh's): a sheath and the hilt with its blade sit at the belt (`root`); draw() carries the hilt to the hand bone for a strike (the blade shows, the sheath stays), sheathe() puts it back
- `features/art/view/model_clips.gd`: Drives a MANUAL AnimationPlayer
- `features/art/view/model_materials.gd`: The materials of live 3D characters: every surface (body, eyes, brows, hair, garments, the hilt) is a ShaderMaterial of character_skin.gdshader, so the painted light of the look reaches all of them through `materials()` (PaintedLook feeds the shared light uniforms), and one `set_all` call drives the flash, desat and glow of the whole character
- `features/art/view/model_move.gd`: What a model's body does on the ground: the ground speed it is really moving at (measured from its own position, so animation and feet agree whoever moves it), the yaw it eases toward at the model's turn speed, and the lean into an acceleration
- `features/art/view/model_parts.gd`: Puts one ModelPartDef on a rig: hair or a rigid mesh from its glTF, a lathed garment, a sleeve capsule or the jambiyah, each on a BoneAttachment3D so it follows the bone through every animation
- `features/art/view/model_react.gd`: What a live 3D character does in answer to the battle's cues, on its materials and on `visual.body`: the hit flash, the revive glow, the knocked-out tint, the small squash of a hit (squash lives on the facade's body node, never on bones) and the victory hop
- `features/art/view/model_rig.gd`: Builds one skinned character under a holder node from its ModelDef: the glTF body (scaled to height_m), its painted materials, the parts it wears on BoneAttachment3D nodes, and a MANUAL AnimationPlayer that carries the shared Quaternius animation library (the same 65-bone rig as the stand-in bodies; a body with other bone axes names a `pose_source` that plays the clips hidden and PoseFollow retargets; the library scene is loaded once and only its AnimationLibrary is kept)
- `features/art/view/model_source.gd`: The live 3D source of a CharacterVisual (docs/design/characters-3d.md): a skinned model (ModelRig) or a rigid one (RigidRig) from the ModelDef with the sprite's id
- `features/art/view/model_weapon.gd`: The grandfather's jambiyah in use: drawn from the belt into the hand when a strike begins (the weapon trail starts tracking its hilt and its point), an arc smear on the impact frame, sheathed and the trail released when the clip ends
- `features/art/view/node_scan.gd`: Finds nodes inside an imported scene by walking its children: every node of a class (the skeleton, the meshes) and the chain of nodes from the root down to one of them (to multiply their transforms)
- `features/art/view/pixel_motion.gd`: The body-shape motions of a pixel character (PixelSource): whole-body squash and stretch (`pulse`), the cast crouch, the victory hop, the hit flash, knocked out and revive
- `features/art/view/pixel_source.gd`: The pixel-art source of a CharacterVisual (today's look, unchanged): a lit, billboarded quad with the sprite's texture (nearest filtering), idle breathing, the walk bob with squash and stretch, the lean into the move and dust at the feet
- `features/art/view/pose_follow.gd`: Retargets at run time: a hidden source body with the library's rig plays the clips, and every frame each target bone of the same name takes the source bone's model-space rotation times a constant offset (PoseMatch), so a body with other bone axes and rest pose (Feras's Rodin models) moves like the library
- `features/art/view/rigid_rig.gd`: A model that is not skinned: a few rigid parts moved by code (the survey drone: its Rodin hull)
- `features/art/view/visual_source.gd`: What draws a CharacterVisual
- `features/art/view/weapon_smear.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/weapon_trail.gd`: The weapon's swing in the air: a ribbon between two tracked points (hilt and the blade's point) that fades along its age, and an arc smear card (a crescent) flashed on the strike frame
- `features/audio/defs/audio_rules_def.gd`: Mixer and behaviour numbers of the AudioDirector (content/audio/rules.json): bus volumes, voice pools, music fade and duck, hit weight, text blip rate, item chime boost per rarity, and which sound each move uses
- `features/audio/defs/music_def.gd`: One music track (content/audio/music.json): its file, volume, whether it loops, and an optional fallback track
- `features/audio/defs/screen_music_def.gd`: Maps one screen id (from the Screens stack) to the music track id it plays while open
- `features/audio/defs/sound_def.gd`: One sound effect (content/audio/sounds.json): file variants (one is picked each play), the bus it plays on, its volume, a random pitch range so repeats differ and whether it ducks the music (stingers)
- `features/audio/logic/music_logic.gd`: Pure rules for music playback: fallback resolution when audio files are missing, and mapping screen ids
- `features/audio/logic/music_stack.gd`: Pure stack of open screen ids deciding which music track plays (content/audio/screen_music.json)
- `features/audio/logic/sound_logic.gd`: Pure sound rules: which variant to play, which sound a move uses and the item chime boost for a rarity
- `features/audio/tests/test_audio.gd`: Audio: every sound and music entry is well formed, every sfx file exists, every vfx id has a sound, the pure sound rules hold, and the AudioDirector builds its buses, plays headless and skips missing music
- `features/audio/tests/test_music_choices.gd`: The owner's music choices (DECISIONS 2026-10-22): menus and the herb stall keep the area music (no screen maps them), every patrol names one of the three battle themes and all three are used, and every track's file exists
- `features/audio/tests/test_music_contexts.gd`: Tests for music contexts: pure stack resolution across all branches, missing file fallback resolution, validation of screen_music definitions, pause process mode, and track resume positions
- `features/audio/tests/test_sound_ids.gd`: Sound ids: every id the code asks the AudioDirector for exists in sounds.json with existing files, and the synthesized Arc Discharge files are 44.1 kHz mono, 0.6-0.9 s long and peak under -1 dBFS
- `features/audio/view/music_deck.gd`: The music side of the AudioDirector: two players so one track crossfades into the next, a duck under stingers, and a pure stack of screen music contexts (content/audio/screen_music.json)
- `features/combat/defs/action_def.gd`: One battle technique: its cost, power, who it targets, and what it does to the timeline (cast speed, recovery, knockback, cancel)
- `features/combat/defs/arena_def.gd`: A battle arena: a painted roof built as a sibling of the exploring area, far from it (origin), so the fight never shares space with the rooftop
- `features/combat/defs/battle_camera_def.gd`: The cinematic battle camera (content/combat/camera.json): the low pose it swoops to from the exploration camera, the gentle idle drift, how far it follows the acting side, the push-in on big moves and the victory pose
- `features/combat/defs/battle_rules_def.gd`: The tunable numbers of one battle ruleset: damage and heal formula factors, SP gain, the stall guard, start ranges and the two thresholds BattleAI uses for heals and guards
- `features/combat/defs/battle_view_def.gd`: Layout and pacing numbers of the battle screen (content/combat/view.json): camera, where each formation slot stands, ticks per frame, hit-stop and banner times, floating-text sizes, HUD sizes and colours
- `features/combat/defs/combatant_def.gd`: One kind of fighter (a party member or an enemy type): base stats and the actions it can use
- `features/combat/defs/encounter_def.gd`: One battle setup: which enemies stand in which formation slots, which slots the party takes, and the guaranteed rewards (equippable loot ids, riyal and consumables, no randomness) granted after a win, and its music
- `features/combat/defs/juice_def.gd`: The "feel" numbers of a battle (content/combat/juice.json): how hard hitstop freezes, how the BREAK flash and the damage numbers pop and bounce, how a camera shake decays
- `features/combat/defs/status_def.gd`: One status effect: how long it lasts and how it changes timeline speed, interrupt immunity and the damage the afflicted unit takes (guarded: 0.6 means 40% less)
- `features/combat/defs/vfx_def.gd`: One battle effect kind (content/combat/vfx.json, id = an ActionDef.VFX_KINDS entry): when the hit lands, the hitstop and camera shake / push it earns, and the layers of pooled sprites it paints
- `features/combat/defs/vfx_layer.gd`: One layer of a VfxDef: `count` sprites of one texture that start at an anchor (plus an offset), grow from size to size_end, drift or travel, spin and fade
- `features/combat/harness/balance.gd`: Balance harness: seeded battles per gear pairing with BattleAI playing both sides, one table
- `features/combat/harness/battle_loader.gd`: Gathers the battle content from a loaded ContentDB (passed in as a Node) and builds ready-to-run BattleSims for the default encounter
- `features/combat/harness/item_policy.gd`: The balance harness's opt-in herb use (docs/design/economy.md section 9): a white herb on a downed hero, a pink herb on the living hero below 40% HP, a yellow herb when a hero cannot pay for his cheapest move
- `features/combat/logic/battle_action_rules.gd`: Move uses per battle, miss roll for confused units, and status cures for BattleSim and BattleResolver
- `features/combat/logic/battle_ai.gd`: The one battle policy (enemies in play, both sides in the balance harness), in this order: 1
- `features/combat/logic/battle_items.gd`: The Items command of a battle (docs/design/economy.md section 5)
- `features/combat/logic/battle_outcome.gd`: What a finished battle hands back: result (victory, defeat, retry, load, title), the party's vitals and bag after the fight, and the rewards (money, equippable items, consumables) still to be applied to GameState by the Router
- `features/combat/logic/battle_request.gd`: What the Router hands to a battle: encounter, arena, ambush, seed, party order, and the pre-battle snapshot (vitals, bag, money) that "Retry fight" restores
- `features/combat/logic/battle_resolver.gd`: Resolves one landed act (docs/design/combat.md, "Resolving an action"): targets, damage or heal per target, timeline effect per hit, status, SP gain, regen, status turns
- `features/combat/logic/battle_setup.gd`: Everything BattleSim.create_from needs for one fight, in one object: the built party (in party order, one CombatantDef per hero) and the enemies with their formation slots, the rules and move tables, the carried vitals and bag, the gear snapshot, the seed, the ambush, which encounter and arena, and the stage anchor
- `features/combat/logic/battle_sim.gd`: One battle (docs/design/combat.md): builds the units, steps the Timeline one tick at a time, asks the player (heroes) or BattleAI (enemies) for choices, resolves acts and decides victory or defeat
- `features/combat/logic/battle_targets.gd`: Who can do what in a battle: a unit's moves, which of them it can pay for, and who a move may target
- `features/combat/logic/formation.gd`: Two rows per side: slots 0-1 are the vanguard, 2-3 the rearguard, and slot n+2 stands behind slot n
- `features/combat/logic/hud_layout.gd`: Pure screen-rectangle maths for the battle HUD: the box around projected points, where a panel may sit beside a fighter without covering any fighter, which fighter the mouse points at, and how an info card fades
- `features/combat/logic/item_action.gd`: A consumable as a battle cast: an ActionDef built from a ConsumableDef, so the timeline treats it like any move (cast speed, recovery, the cast bar, interrupts)
- `features/combat/logic/timeline.gd`: Grandia-style initiative track (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, "Combat")
- `features/combat/logic/timeline_event.gd`: One thing that happened in a battle, for the battle view and logs: what, who, a value (timeline position, damage, status turns) and a detail id (the action for damage, the status for status/status_ended)
- `features/combat/logic/unit_letters.gd`: Tells apart units of the same kind on one side: two Concession Enforcers are A and B, a lone unit has no letter
- `features/combat/logic/unit_state.gd`: One fighter during one battle: the numbers that change (hp, timeline position, the action being cast), built from a read-only CombatantDef
- `features/combat/tests/battle_probe.gd`: Test helper (not a test): hand-made fighters, moves and battles with exact numbers, and loops that play a BattleSim until an event kind appears
- `features/combat/tests/fake_clip_source.gd`: A stand-in VisualSource for battle view tests: a model-like source of a known size that sends clip events only when the test says so, and records what the battle asked of it (clips, facings, hit pauses, collapses)
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_balance.gd`: Balance harness for Abu Nabil duel: 200 seeded battles with policy AI on both sides
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_combat.gd`: Abu Nabil combat rules: miss rolls for confused units, status cures, uses per battle, and boss AI policy
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_spar.gd`: Abu Nabil Spar tests: practice BattleRequest flags, reverse_stab suppression on duels, snapshot restoration on win/loss with zero payout, and spar defeat without defeat screen
- `features/combat/tests/test_action_def.gd`: ActionDef new fields: target, heal, revive, vfx (validated on load), and the shipped actions: every one has a vfx from the agreed list, and the tech moves have the shape the design asks for
- `features/combat/tests/test_arena.gd`: The painted arena: the def points at real content, the builder makes the roof, the parapet, the props, the lights and the city, the arena camera sits low with its own depth of field, and the party stands right, the enemies left
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_ai_support.gd`: BattleAI with support moves: heal an ally under 40% HP, revive the fallen, guard before a big enemy cast, and never waste a heal or buff when nobody needs it
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_camera.gd`: The cinematic battle camera: it frames the stage from a low angle (12-16 degrees down), starts at the exploration camera and swoops to the battle pose, then drifts, follows, pushes in, shakes and glides to the victory pose, all from content/combat/camera.json
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_flow.gd`: How a fight starts and ends: carried vitals fill the bars, the end panel shows the riyal, the shatter warp skips cleanly without a frame, the Defeat screen opens on a loss and its three picks leave the fight (retry, load, title)
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_hud_style.gd`: The restyled battle HUD keeps its behaviour and gains: tags on the command buttons, gradient bars in the party panel, the brass timeline track, and rarity-coloured spoils on the victory panel (only items not owned yet)
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_hud_v2.gd`: Battle HUD v2 basics (kept in v3): the thin timeline sits on top at the view's size and its icons come from content (disc fallback), each hero has a strip and the acting hero a card, and the hint strip is there
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_hud_v3.gd`: Battle HUD v3: at rest only a thin timeline and a slim strip under each hero; a hero's turn adds a card and a compact menu beside them; pointing shows an info card that fades; targeting names the target on the top bar; hits pulse a hero's strip and reveal a foe's; and at 1920x1080 nothing the HUD draws at rest covers a fighter
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_interrupt.gd`: T4: a cancel move landing on a casting enemy interrupts it (back to INTERRUPT_POS) inside BattleSim
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_item_menu.gd`: The Items entry of the command menu and its list: greyed with no herbs, rows with free counts, then the targets, back at each level, and a committed herb is a reserved cast on the timeline
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_items.gd`: The Items command in the sim: a herb is reserved when chosen (two heroes cannot share the last one), cast at its cast speed, consumed at ACT with the real amounts, and refunded when the target is no longer valid, when the cast is cut, or when the user falls first
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_menu_support.gd`: The command menu with tech moves: an ally move lists the allies (not the foes), self and all-moves skip the target list and commit at once, and the party is built from saved gear
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_outcome.gd`: The battle contract: BattleSetup carries carried vitals and the bag into units, hero ids come from the party list, BattleOutcome reports vitals after (a downed hero stands at ko_stand_hp after a victory only) and the bag, and the speed / melee numbers come from the battle rules
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_perks.gd`: Perks in battle (sp_per_act, hp_regen, start_bonus, bonus_knockback), Perks.apply on a fighter copy, and the rarity rule that only Rare and above may carry a perk
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_rules.gd`: T5: damage, SP, cover, retargeting and status turns follow docs/design/combat.md
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_sim.gd`: BattleSim: unit ids, determinism (T1), every battle ends (T2), refused choices, event order, stall guard
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_stage.gd`: BattleStage headless (instant mode): it builds with 5 fighters, 5 timeline icons and a camera; an auto-played battle ends once; the command menu opens for a waiting hero, lists that hero's moves and the sim's valid targets, and choosing through its confirm path calls sim.choose; enemy intent labels; tips; the end panel
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_start.gd`: Starting positions and ambushes, the first-hit-only knockback bonus, downed units, and lands_before()
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_status.gd`: T5 (statuses): applied by a move, refreshed on re-apply, one turn lost per act of the afflicted unit, and the cast-speed / knockback-bonus numbers of a CombatantDef
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_tech.gd`: Tech moves: ally / self / all-target moves, heals (never above max HP, downed allies stay down unless the move revives), the guarded and overclocked statuses, and the damage-taken multiplier
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_view3d.gd`: The battle view is ready for 3D models: it waits on the actor's clip events (never a timer), faces by direction with a lean toward the camera and never a negative scale, freezes both fighters at impact, places effects, numbers and markers from the characters' anchors, spaces lunges by width, plays the ko state, and keeps SceneTreeTimers out
- `features/combat/tests/test_formation.gd`: Formation rows: cover and melee multipliers
- `features/combat/tests/test_hud_layout.gd`: HudLayout (pure rect maths) and UnitLetters: boxes around points, panels that dodge fighters, which fighter the mouse points at, the info card's fade, and the A / B letters of same-kind units
- `features/combat/tests/test_item_policy.gd`: ItemPolicy (balance harness): herbs only when the bag has them, deterministic, battles still end
- `features/combat/tests/test_pause_safety.gd`: Pausing the game stops battle waits and cancels a hitstop (a SceneTreeTimer would keep running during a pause)
- `features/combat/tests/test_reverse_stab.gd`: The reverse stab: only when the party was ambushed, Zayd strikes the lowest-slot living enemy first
- `features/combat/tests/test_timeline.gd`: Timeline rules: command pause, cast and act, interrupts, knockback limits, determinism
- `features/combat/tests/test_vfx.gd`: Battle effects: every ActionDef vfx kind has data, every texture paints, the effect player builds and plays each kind (single target and all foes) without errors and gives its sprites back to the pool, and the juice numbers (hitstop, shake, zoom) come from data and rank heavy above light
- `features/combat/view/arena_builder.gd`: Builds a battle arena from its ArenaDef: a painted roof slab whose top is at the arena origin, a parapet round three sides (the fourth is the camera's), the dressing (props, lanterns, the city behind) and the look's key light, placed far from the exploring area (content/combat/arenas.json)
- `features/combat/view/arena_dressing.gd`: The things standing on and around an arena's roof, built with the world's own helpers so the painted look applies: props (PropBuilder; no collision, nothing walks here), the lanterns' light (AreaLights, a few real OmniLights plus fake pools), and the city behind (SkylineBuilder) centred on the roof
- `features/combat/view/battle_action_player.gd`: Plays the swing of one move: the camera leans toward the actor, the actor plays its clip (attack, cast or item) while a melee actor anticipates and dashes, and the call returns when the CLIP says the hit lands (its `impact` event, never a timer; a ranged move then waits out its effect's flight)
- `features/combat/view/battle_camera.gd`: The cinematic battle camera
- `features/combat/view/battle_camera_rig.gd`: Builds a BattleStage's camera: the Camera3D with the arena's Environment and the cinematic BattleCamera that moves it, and the painted look's ink outline and grade on top
- `features/combat/view/battle_command_menu.gd`: The compact command menu (in the turn panel, beside the hero) for the hero waiting at COMMAND: first one Button per move (unaffordable ones disabled; name, SP cost, a "cancels" / target tag; the focused move's description below), then one Button per valid target (foes or allies; self and all-moves skip this list)
- `features/combat/view/battle_demo.gd`: Battle view demo: a plain floor in the accepted HD-2D look and a BattleStage fighting the rooftop patrol (swift hilt, keen blade, seed 7, ambushed so the reverse stab shows)
- `features/combat/view/battle_demo.tscn`: scene
- `features/combat/view/battle_end_panel.gd`: The end-of-battle panel in the middle of the screen
- `features/combat/view/battle_ending.gd`: How a fight leaves the screen
- `features/combat/view/battle_event_player.gd`: Plays a batch of TimelineEvents one after another with the animation each one deserves: the swing and its effect (BattleActionPlayer), the flinch, hitstop and popping numbers of a hit, the BREAK! stamp of a cut cast, collapses and revives
- `features/combat/view/battle_event_targets.gd`: Finds unit targets touched by a move from the timeline events that follow it (hits, heals, misses)
- `features/combat/view/battle_fighters.gd`: The 3D side of a battle: one CharacterVisual per unit on the stage, popping damage / heal numbers and status text, the BREAK! stamp, intent labels over casting enemies, and the bouncing target marker
- `features/combat/view/battle_hero_card.gd`: The acting hero's full card, on top of the turn panel: name, HP and SP with numbers
- `features/combat/view/battle_hud.gd`: The battle HUD (v3), built in code and minimal at rest: a thin timeline on top (with the chosen target's name), a slim vitals strip under each hero's feet, and nothing else
- `features/combat/view/battle_info_card.gd`: The small card beside a fighter that is pointed at (mouse over it, or the focus on it while targeting)
- `features/combat/view/battle_item_menu.gd`: The Items list of the command menu (in the turn panel, in place of the move list): one row per herb the bag holds (name, the count still free, its effect), then the targets of the picked herb (the party herb skips them)
- `features/combat/view/battle_juice.gd`: Hitstop and camera shake for the battle view
- `features/combat/view/battle_labels.gd`: Builders for the 3D bits of the battle screen: billboard text (damage numbers, status text, enemy intent) and the target marker
- `features/combat/view/battle_menu_chips.gd`: The small tags on the right edge of a command-menu button: SP cost (cyan), "cancels" (magenta), the target scope of a self / all move, and for a target the HP and a "will interrupt" warning
- `features/combat/view/battle_notices.gd`: The words the HUD says to the player: a compact banner in the upper middle ("Interrupted!") that fades, the one-time tip under the top bar, and the key hint strip at the bottom (shown only while a menu is open)
- `features/combat/view/battle_numbers.gd`: The pop-up text of a battle: damage and heal numbers that pop in with an overshoot, bounce up and fade (bigger for heavy hits, green for heals), and the BREAK! stamp over a unit whose cast was cut
- `features/combat/view/battle_rects.gd`: Where each fighter stands on the screen: the box of a CharacterVisual (its width and height from the facade) is projected with the battle camera and boxed again, so panels, strips and the mouse can steer clear of the fighters whatever the art is (sprite, model)
- `features/combat/view/battle_runner.gd`: One fight, away from the exploring area: builds the arena from the request, the sim from content and the saved gear, the BattleStage beside it, and reports the stage's result
- `features/combat/view/battle_shatter.gd`: The warp into a fight: the last frame of the area breaks into qamariya-glass shards that fall away and uncover the arena (battle_shatter.gdshader)
- `features/combat/view/battle_shatter.gdshader`
- `features/combat/view/battle_stage.gd`: The battle screen (wait mode): places the fighters and the camera, runs the HUD, steps a BattleSim a few ticks per physics frame and plays the resulting events
- `features/combat/view/battle_strips.gd`: The resting vitals of the battle: a slim BattleUnitStrip under each hero's feet (always there) and under a foe while it was hit lately or is pointed at (it fades after the view's delay)
- `features/combat/view/battle_style.gd`: Small builders for the battle screen's look (labels, bars, names, head icons)
- `features/combat/view/battle_timeline_bar.gd`: The thin top bar of the battle: a slim brass track from 0 to ACT_POINT with a COMMAND mark and a tinted cast zone (BattleTrackArt, compact), one small head icon per living unit at its timeline position (foes above the track, the party below it), and at the left the name of the chosen target
- `features/combat/view/battle_track_art.gd`: The painted brass track of the timeline bar: dark glass, brass rails, tick marks, the tinted cast zone, a gypsum zigzag frieze along the bottom, the COMMAND mark (a brass line with diamonds) and an end cap at ACT
- `features/combat/view/battle_turn_panel.gd`: What a hero's turn shows, in one framed panel: that hero's full card over the compact command menu (or the herb list), placed beside the hero on the side where no fighter stands
- `features/combat/view/battle_unit_strip.gd`: One slim vitals strip under a fighter's feet: a name initial (the letter for same-kind foes) and a thin HP bar, for a hero also a thinner SP bar
- `features/combat/view/battle_vitals.gd`: A name line over a thin HP bar and an optional thin SP bar, with the numbers beside them when wanted
- `features/combat/view/clip_wait.gd`: Waits for a named clip event of one CharacterVisual (&"impact": the hit lands, &"end": the clip is over)
- `features/combat/view/pause_wait.gd`: The one pause-safe wait of the battle view
- `features/combat/view/vfx_player.gd`: Paints a VfxDef: turns each layer into pooled VfxSprites around the actor and the target(s) and moves them every frame (no tweens, no allocation once the pool is warm)
- `features/combat/view/vfx_sprite.gd`: One pooled effect quad
- `features/combat/view/vfx_sprite.gdshader`
- `features/combat/view/vfx_textures.gd`: Procedurally painted effect textures (no files): crisp hard-edged pixel shapes (a bright core and a darker rim, one-bit alpha) plus one soft glow
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_choice.gd`: A player choice at the end of a dialogue line: text key, next dialogue (or "end"), and effects
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_def.gd`: A conversation: an ordered list of lines (speaker, expression, text key)
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_line.gd`: One spoken line: who says it, with which expression, localization key, and optional choices
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_style_def.gd`: Look and timing of the dialogue box (fractions of the screen, pixels, colours, speed) and the pixel marks (brows, mouth) that make the stand-in portraits show an expression
- `features/dialogue/defs/speaker_def.gd`: One speaking character: name key, name colour, the pixel sprite id, and where the face sits on that sprite (sprite pixels)
- `features/dialogue/defs/talk_def.gd`: Maps a place id to its first dialogue, after-battle dialogue and ordered chats
- `features/dialogue/dialogue_effects.gd`: Applies side effects from dialogue choices: set_flag, open_shop, start_battle, give_item
- `features/dialogue/logic/dialogue_run.gd`: Steps through a DialogueDef one line at a time
- `features/dialogue/logic/standin_portrait.gd`: Builds a stand-in portrait Image for a speaker without painted art: a soft glow in the speaker colour, a disc in that colour and brow and mouth marks per expression
- `features/dialogue/logic/talk_picker.gd`: Pure picker that selects the next dialogue for a talk place from saved flags: 1
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_abu_nabil_haggle.gd`: Abu Nabil Haggle and Shop tests: Haggle dialogue branches A/B/C/D, flag side effects, walk-away safety, win dialogue, post-win menu gating, and shop prices before/after win
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue.gd`: Dialogue: T8 (every line has a known speaker, one of 4 expressions, a translating text key), DialogueRun stepping, the object-list reader, the stand-in portraits, and DialogueBox playing to the end once
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue_choices.gd`: Dialogue choices test: DialogueChoice def parsing, DialogueRun choice exposure and advance blocking, DialogueEffects execution, and DialogueBox button selection
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue_v2.gd`: Dialogue v2 (Hades II style): nameplate with epithet, typed text, portrait slide on a speaker change, Cease, the layout sizes from the UI style, and stand-in portraits that no longer touch sprite pixels
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_talk_defs.gd`: Checks that talks.json is well formed and all referenced dialogue ids exist in ContentDB
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_talk_picker.gd`: Tests for TalkPicker: first dialogue, after-battle dialogue on victory, chat sequence and wrapping, battle interruption resuming chats, and defensive fallbacks
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_box.gd`: The dialogue box, Hades II style: a big portrait slides in when the speaker changes, a nameplate sits on the box, lines are typed out, and choice buttons offer branching dialogue
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_choice_list.gd`: Manages the focusable button list for dialogue choices
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_demo.gd`: Manual check: plays the workshop_first dialogue over a plain background (F6 in the editor)
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_demo.tscn`: scene
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_layout.gd`: Builds the dialogue box's controls in code (Hades II style; sizes from the UI style, laid out for 1920x1080): a big portrait at the left that slides in, an ornate glass text box at the bottom right with a frieze, a nameplate tab on the box's top edge (name in brass, epithet under it) and the button hints
- `features/dialogue/view/portraits.gd`: Finds the portrait texture for (speaker, expression): res://assets/portraits/<speaker>_<expression>.png when it exists (loaded straight from the file, the "keep" importer needs no import step), else the speaker's painted neutral (a painted face beats a stand-in), else a stand-in disc with the expression's brows and mouth (StandinPortrait)
- `features/equipment/logic/equipment_options.gd`: Pure rules of the equipment screen: which slots a hero has, which OWNED items fit a slot (best rarity first), which items a hero wears now, the fighter built from a staged set of items, and writing a staged set into the saved equipment through Inventory.equip
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment.gd`: The equipment screen: the pure options rules (owned items only, rarer first, per hero and slot), the screen listing only owned items in rarity colours, staging, Confirm writing every slot through Inventory.equip, back changing nothing, and the stat comparison
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_data.gd`: What the equipment screen needs from ContentDB, read once: every equippable by id, the perks, the rarity order, and each hero's start loadout (heroes in loadout order)
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_demo.gd`: Manual check: opens the equipment screen over a plain background (F6 in the editor) with a few owned items
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_demo.tscn`: scene
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_detail.gd`: The right-hand side of the equipment screen: the focused item (name in its rarity colour, tag, text, perk and the tech moves it teaches) above the stat comparison (base, with the staged kit, an up / down arrow)
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_item_button.gd`: Builds one owned item as a menu button: its name in the rarity colour, the rarity tag and an "Equipped" mark on the right
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_page.gd`: The equipment layout: title and hero tabs on top, the slot lists on the left, the item detail and stat comparison on the right, Confirm with the back hint at the bottom
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_screen.gd`: The equipment screen (the bench): a tab per hero (Zayd: hilt, blade, prosthetic; Bilqis: prosthetic), the OWNED items of each slot with rarity colours and tags, the perk and tech moves of the focused item, and the stat comparison base vs
- `features/items/defs/chest_def.gd`: A chest holding an equippable (an id of a hilt, blade or prosthetic), riyal and/or consumables; at least one
- `features/items/defs/consumable_def.gd`: A stackable item used from the bag, in the field or in battle (feathered herbs, the qishr cup)
- `features/items/defs/count_map.gd`: Reads an optional {"id": count} JSON object (rewards, the start bag) as {StringName: int}, each count 1 or more
- `features/items/defs/economy_rules_def.gd`: The money and rest numbers (content/economy/rules.json, id "default"): start purse and bag, the cap, the repeat-win payout share, the HP a downed hero stands up with after a victory, the patrol respawn guards
- `features/items/defs/equip_def.gd`: Shared base of everything a hero can wear or wield (hilt, blade, prosthetic): names, a rarity tier and an optional perk (Rare and above only; rules in docs/design/prosthetics.md)
- `features/items/defs/perk_def.gd`: One perk an item can carry: a kind that battle logic implements and an amount
- `features/items/defs/rarity_def.gd`: One rarity tier: its name, display colour, sort order, whether it is story-only (never loot) and whether gear of this tier may carry a perk
- `features/items/defs/shop_def.gd`: A stall: who keeps it, her greeting and the consumable ids on sale (price and sell come from the ConsumableDef)
- `features/items/item_service.gd`: Uses a consumable on the party outside battle against GameState: FieldUse does the rules on copies, this writes the bag and the carried vitals back only when the use worked
- `features/items/logic/bag.gd`: The party's stackable consumables: counts per id plus RESERVATIONS made by pending battle casts
- `features/items/logic/chests.gd`: Chest rules: opening gives the item once, and the opened state is a saved flag
- `features/items/logic/field_use.gd`: Using a consumable outside battle, pure: the item must be usable in the field, aimed at living allies, and must change something (a full hero is refused)
- `features/items/logic/gear.gd`: Builds a hero's fighter from the shared base plus worn gear: base -> hilt -> blade -> prosthetic -> perks (caps are applied by each step)
- `features/items/logic/holdings.gd`: What rewards are paid into: riyal, the consumable Bag, the unique-item inventory and the flags
- `features/items/logic/inventory.gd`: Which unique items the party owns and whether a hero may wear one in a slot
- `features/items/logic/item_effect.gd`: What a consumable does to one hero: gains() computes the real change from current numbers (never past the maximum, a herb never helps a downed hero, a white herb only a downed one); apply() writes it into carried vitals
- `features/items/logic/perks.gd`: Applies perks to a fighter
- `features/items/logic/reward_result.gd`: What a reward really changed: riyal added (after the cap), the equippables that were new, the consumables that fit in the bag, and riyal that came from herbs which did not fit (sold at their sell price)
- `features/items/logic/rewards.gd`: Rewards for a won battle or an opened chest, paid straight into a Holdings
- `features/items/logic/shop.gd`: The herb stall's rules, pure: buy (refused when the stock lacks it, the purse is short or the stack is full) and sell (bag consumables only, never reserved ones; gear is not a consumable so it can never be sold)
- `features/items/logic/shop_result.gd`: What one buy or sell did (or why it did not): reason is &"" on success, else one of Shop.SHORT_MONEY etc
- `features/items/logic/vitals.gd`: Carried HP and SP per hero: {hero id: {"hp": int, "sp": int}}
- `features/items/reward_applier.gd`: Pays rewards (Rewards) into GameState and announces them: item_obtained per new equippable, item_gained per herb stack, money_changed for the riyal
- `features/items/shop_service.gd`: Runs the stall against GameState: Shop does the rules on a Holdings copy, this takes the copy back and announces it
- `features/items/tests/fixtures/bad_items/hilts.json`: content: hilt x3
- `features/items/tests/fixtures/bad_items/rarities.json`: content: rarity x2
- `features/items/tests/test_bag.gd`: Bag: stack caps with overflow, removal, and reservations (two heroes cannot both claim the last herb; release gives the claim back; consume uses it up)
- `features/items/tests/test_inventory.gd`: Inventory (unique owned items, equip checks per slot), chests (open once, saved flag) and the item_obtained signal on the EventBus
- `features/items/tests/test_items.gd`: Rarity tiers and the shipped items: six tiers with the owner's colours, every equippable has a real rarity, ids are unique across hilts / blades / prosthetics, the Heirloom is story-only and never loot, and bad content (an unknown rarity, a bad colour) is reported
- `features/items/tests/test_rewards.gd`: Rewards: the first win pays everything and sets patrol_paid_<id>, a repeat win pays half the riyal and nothing else, herbs over the stack turn into riyal, the purse has a cap, a chest pays once
- `features/items/tests/test_shop.gd`: The herb stall: buy and sell rules and their edge cases (economy.md section 9), the ShopService purse signal, and using consumables in the field (FieldUse, ItemService)
- `features/jambiyah/defs/blade_def.gd`: A jambiyah blade: adds to attack, adds knockback to every hit the wielder lands, adds weight
- `features/jambiyah/defs/hilt_def.gd`: A jambiyah hilt: adds to agility, multiplies cast speed, adds weight, and grants exactly one move
- `features/jambiyah/defs/loadout_def.gd`: A hero's starting gear: which hilt, blade and prosthetic they own and wear at the start (each optional)
- `features/jambiyah/logic/jambiyah.gd`: Builds Zayd's fighter from a base CombatantDef plus one hilt and one blade (docs/design/combat.md)
- `features/jambiyah/logic/loadout.gd`: Which gear a hero wears: the saved choice per slot ("<hero>.<part>" in GameState.equipment), else the starting gear
- `features/jambiyah/logic/stat_row.gd`: One line of the workshop comparison: label key, value now (base) and value with the chosen pair
- `features/jambiyah/logic/workshop_stats.gd`: The comparison rows the equipment screen shows: base fighter against the fighter built by Jambiyah.equip
- `features/jambiyah/tests/test_jambiyah.gd`: T3: every hilt + blade pairing gives a different Zayd stat sets, inside the timeline caps; each hilt adds exactly one move; the shared base definition is never changed
- `features/jambiyah/tests/test_loadout.gd`: The loadout fallback: a hero wears the saved item per slot, else the start loadout
- `features/prosthetics/defs/prosthetic_def.gd`: A high-tech prosthetic: one slot per hero
- `features/prosthetics/logic/prosthetics.gd`: Merges a prosthetic into a fighter (docs/design/prosthetics.md), like Jambiyah.equip: stat adds, then the granted moves, then the caps
- `features/prosthetics/tests/test_prosthetics.gd`: Prosthetics: the merge (base -> hilt -> blade -> prosthetic -> perks -> caps) builds new fighters and never touches the shared defs; each hero's prosthetics grant 1-2 tech moves; a prosthetic fits only its wearer
- `features/prototype/prototype_battle_flow.gd`: Handles battle conclusion effects for the prototype (patrol wins, Abu Nabil boss and spar)
- `features/prototype/prototype_main.gd`: The playable prototype's composition root: builds the rooftop, the workshop dialogue and menu, the title overlay, area title card and loot banners, registers the rooftop with the Router and wires the features' public signals
- `features/prototype/prototype_main.tscn`: scene
- `features/prototype/rooftop_port.gd`: The rooftop as the Router sees it: hide and disable it during a battle (it stays in the tree, so its awaits, signals and camera keep working), bring it back, and move the party for unstuck and loading
- `features/prototype/tests/flow_harness.gd`: Test helpers for the game flow: a PrototypeMain whose battles run instantly with the AI choosing for the heroes, a patrol touch, a scratch save folder and a Router that records reloads instead of reloading the scene
- `features/prototype/tests/test_prototype.gd`: T6: the prototype main scene builds headless with rooftop, dialogue box and workshop menu; a simulated patrol touch starts a battle and stops exploring; an auto-played battle ends and walking resumes with the patrol reset; retry starts a fresh battle; the first workshop visit plays the talk, then the menu; later visits skip the talk
- `features/prototype/tests/test_router_area.gd`: The Router outside battles: the play-time clock (not while paused or at the title, real seconds under a slowed time scale), busy and can_save, unstuck to the last place the player stood still, and the saved chest state
- `features/prototype/tests/test_router_battle.gd`: The Router's battle round trip: the area is hidden and stopped while the arena fights, then restored; Retry and defeat restore the pre-battle snapshot; vitals and herbs carry (a downed hero stands up after a victory); the first win pays everything and a repeat pays half
- `features/prototype/tests/test_smoke_flow.gd`: Smoke test of the whole flow, headless through the Router: a new game, a fight on auto-play, the outcome applied to GameState, a save, a load that restores exactly that state
- `features/prototype/tests/test_talk_interact.gd`: Interaction test: walking up to herb_seller and confirming plays abu_nabil_first on the first visit, and abu_nabil_chat_1 on the next visit; sabil plays party_sabil_first before opening screen
- `features/ui/defs/backdrop_def.gd`: Backdrop definition for full-screen menu backgrounds
- `features/ui/defs/ui_style_def.gd`: The look of every menu and HUD (content/ui/style.json): three font files, named colours (c_*), sizes in pixels at 1920x1080 (s_*) and times in seconds (t_*)
- `features/ui/logic/pause_logic.gd`: Pure rules of the pause menu: which entries show and in what order, which ask "are you sure", the vitals of a hero with a missing record (= full), and the play-time clock text
- `features/ui/logic/prompt_glyph.gd`: Pure: the localization key of the button glyph for an action on keyboard or gamepad ("accept" -> Enter / A), and the fade of a world-space interaction prompt with distance
- `features/ui/logic/toast_queue.gd`: Pure: toasts wait in order and are shown one at a time
- `features/ui/tests/node_walk.gd`: Test helper (not a test): every descendant of a node, depth first
- `features/ui/tests/test_items_shop.gd`: The Items and Shop screens on the Screens stack, and the riyal banner of the loot popup
- `features/ui/tests/test_menu_skins.gd`: Menu skins test: backdrops, fallback, child 0, party rows, thumbnails, shop money-after, rects
- `features/ui/tests/test_musnad.gd`: The written language of Sana'a in 2150 is Musnad only: no Arabic script in any CSV, JSON or script; every *_MUSNAD and WORLD_SIGN_* text holds only Musnad letters, spaces and arrows; the Musnad font draws it
- `features/ui/tests/test_pause_menu.gd`: The pause menu rules (PauseLogic) and the screen built from them
- `features/ui/tests/test_popups.gd`: The loot popup (queues item_obtained in order, skippable), the area title card, the title overlay (any key dismisses it once) and the opening shot held on the moon until then
- `features/ui/tests/test_sabil_defeat.gd`: The Sabil question and the Defeat screen: registered ids, focus order, results, back handling
- `features/ui/tests/test_screens.gd`: The Screens stack: push/pop pause the tree and emit game_paused, focus returns to the control that had it, back goes to the top screen, an unhandled menu opens pause only while exploring with nothing open, screens open by id
- `features/ui/tests/test_slot_picker.gd`: Slot picker tests: save mode, overwrite confirmation dialog, load mode, empty slots greyed, and back
- `features/ui/tests/test_title_overlay.gd`: Tests for TitleOverlay: Continue loads the newest slot, Load opens the slot picker, and New Game
- `features/ui/tests/test_ui.gd`: The shared UI look: the style loads completely, the theme builds with every font (Reem Kufi and Amiri for English, Noto Old South Arabian for Musnad), every rarity has a colour, the painted frames have the right size, and the text server lays Musnad out right to left
- `features/ui/tests/test_ui_helpers.gd`: UI v2 helpers: list_row, party_card, money_counter, prompt_strip and its glyph keys, toast queue and host, interaction prompt fade, typed text, the qamariya transition sweep, and the head icons with their disc fallback
- `features/ui/view/area_title_card.gd`: The area title card (centre left, no panel) that fades in when the opening shot ends: the Musnad name big over the English name, a gypsum frieze drawing left to right, a subtitle (place and year), then fading out
- `features/ui/view/character_icons.gd`: Head icons for timeline medallions and party cards
- `features/ui/view/interaction_prompt.gd`: A small glass pill above an object in the world: the interact glyph and a verb ("Drink", "Talk", "Open")
- `features/ui/view/list_row.gd`: One row of a menu list: icon | name (rarity colour) | "x3" count | tag chip on the right
- `features/ui/view/loot_popup.gd`: The "Obtained" banner: listens to EventBus.item_obtained and shows each new item centred high on the screen with its name in the rarity colour, a light sweep for Rare and above and a rarity jingle (AudioDirector.play_item)
- `features/ui/view/menu_backdrop.gd`: Full-screen painted menu backdrop with blur fallback
- `features/ui/view/menu_blur.gdshader`
- `features/ui/view/money_counter.gd`: A pill with the riyal amount in brass
- `features/ui/view/party_card.gd`: A hero card: portrait icon, name, HP and SP bars with numbers
- `features/ui/view/prompt_strip.gd`: The Hades-style button hints along the bottom: "[Enter] Select   [Esc] Back"
- `features/ui/view/screens/choice_screen.gd`: Base of the small centred "pick one" screens (Sabil, Defeat): a framed panel with the Musnad + English title pair and a column of buttons in focus order
- `features/ui/view/screens/confirm_dialog.gd`: A centred Yes/No question over the scrim
- `features/ui/view/screens/defeat_screen.gd`: The defeat screen (Screens id &"defeat"): the arena darkens over t_defeat_fade, then DEFEATED offers Retry fight (default), Load last save (greyed with no save) and Title (asks first)
- `features/ui/view/screens/equipment_host.gd`: Puts the existing EquipmentScreen (the bench, a CanvasLayer with its own open()/closed API) on the Screens stack as the screen &"equipment"
- `features/ui/view/screens/items_screen.gd`: The Items screen (Screens id &"items", opened from the pause menu): the bag on the left, the chosen item's description and effect on the right, and under it the hero picker
- `features/ui/view/screens/items_text.gd`: Item screen wording: the effect line ("HP +120") and a hero's "HP 200 -> 320" preview
- `features/ui/view/screens/pause_hero_row.gd`: One hero row in the pause party panel: face 160x160, name, class, HP/SP bars, KO state
- `features/ui/view/screens/pause_menu.gd`: Pause menu screen: command panel (80,80), info box (80,880), party panel (540,80), prompt strip (0,1020)
- `features/ui/view/screens/pause_party.gd`: Party panel for the pause screen: one row per hero (h 200)
- `features/ui/view/screens/sabil_screen.gd`: The sabil fountain question (Screens id &"sabil"): "Drink to rest? This saves your game and restores everyone." Closes with &"drink" (default) or &"leave" (Not now, or back)
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_cell.gd`: One cell in the shop item grid: 220x170, icon 96, name, price c_brass, rarity glow, sold out dim
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_detail.gd`: Shop detail panel at (840,140) 560x760: icon 160, name, desc, effect, and per-hero comparison
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_grid.gd`: Shop grid panel at (80,140) 720x560: tabs [Buy][Sell] and 3-column items grid
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_keeper_box.gd`: Keeper box: portrait 220x260 and typed greeting in a glass box at (80,720) 620x260
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_party_mini.gd`: Party mini cards panel at (1440,600) 400x300: compact HP and SP bars for each hero
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_screen.gd`: Shop screen: title (80,40), grid (80,140), keeper (80,720), detail (840,140), summary (1440,140), party (1440,600)
- `features/ui/view/screens/shop_summary.gd`: Shop summary panel at (1440,140) 400x420: quantity, owned, price, money after (c_bad when < 0)
- `features/ui/view/screens/slot_detail.gd`: Details panel for the focused save slot: header, thumbnail 440x248, area, party, riyal, play time
- `features/ui/view/screens/slot_picker_screen.gd`: Slot picker screen: title (560,60), 3 slot rows (440,180), details (1380,180), buttons (500,880)
- `features/ui/view/screens/slot_row.gd`: One save slot row: thumbnail 300x170, slot label, area, play time, date, or empty slot
- `features/ui/view/title_overlay.gd`: The game's title over the opening sky: "Qarnaw" in Musnad (big) and Latin with a pulsing "Press any key"
- `features/ui/view/toast_host.gd`: Shows toasts top-centre one at a time (ToastQueue order): fade in, hold t_toast_hold, fade out, next
- `features/ui/view/ui.gd`: Entry point of the shared UI look: the style (content/ui/style.json), the one cached Theme, and small builders (labels, screen roots, the zigzag divider)
- `features/ui/view/ui_boxes.gd`: StyleBox builders for the UI theme: ornate panels (painted nine-patch frames), button states with the warm brass focus glow, and progress-bar tracks and gradient fills
- `features/ui/view/ui_layers.gd`: The one table of CanvasLayer layers (engine draw-order values, so named constants are allowed here)
- `features/ui/view/ui_motion.gd`: UI tweens: they ignore Engine.time_scale (a battle hitstop must not slow a menu) and, bound to a node whose process mode is ALWAYS (every UiScreen), keep running while the tree is paused
- `features/ui/view/ui_ornament.gd`: Procedurally painted UI textures from the UiStyleDef (no image files): the nine-patch frames (a thin brass line, a thin gypsum line inside it and a small diamond in each corner, like the carved plaster of a Sana'a tower-house), and the zigzag frieze band that divides sections
- `features/ui/view/ui_panel.gd`: A framed night-glass panel: gypsum tracery frame (the theme's panel box), an optional title pair (English left in Reem Kufi, Musnad right in dim brass) with a frieze under it, and a `body` column for the content
- `features/ui/view/ui_rarity.gd`: Rarity helpers for every screen: the tier colour (from RarityDef), coloured item names and the small rarity tag
- `features/ui/view/ui_screen.gd`: Base of every full menu (pause, items, shop, confirm, defeat)
- `features/ui/view/ui_stack.gd`: Screen stack (autoload Screens): push/pop UiScreens (each on its own UiLayers layer), pause the tree while one wants it, restore focus when one closes, route `back` / `menu` input, and open the pause menu on `menu` when the game is exploring and nothing is open
- `features/ui/view/ui_sweep.gd`: The qamariya focus sweep: a thin line under a focused control runs red, amber, green, blue, violet (stained glass) from left to right, then rests on brass
- `features/ui/view/ui_theme.gd`: Builds the one Godot Theme every menu and HUD uses: Amiri for reading, Reem Kufi for titles, names and numbers, ornate panels, brass-focus buttons, gradient bars
- `features/ui/view/ui_transition.gd`: The qamariya screen wipe: five stained-glass shards (red, amber, green, blue, violet) drop over the screen one after another, cover it, then lift away
- `features/ui/view/ui_type.gd`: Typed text: a label reveals one character per t_text_char with the typing blip; confirm finishes the line
- `features/world/defs/area_def.gd`: A level as data: equal-width rows of tile characters, a legend (character -> tile id), two markers (S spawn, W workshop bench) that each appear once and stand on floor, and typed places (PlaceDef: stall, sabil, patrols...)
- `features/world/defs/area_problems.gd`: Checks an AreaDef for layout problems: row widths, unmapped tiles, missing markers, out-of-bounds places
- `features/world/defs/building_def.gd`: One Sana'a tower-house as data: footprint (metres), floors (the lowest stone_floors are basalt), window columns per facade, frieze style, qamariya glass letters, lit-window ratio, parapet style and roof extras
- `features/world/defs/camera_preset_def.gd`: Stub (v0.3 registry, filled by the level builder): one named camera pose with its own field of view and depth of field, e.g
- `features/world/defs/camera_rig_def.gd`: Camera language for exploring (content/world/camera.json): intro shots, presets, limits, and follow/framed modes
- `features/world/defs/camera_room_def.gd`: Specification and authored dimensions for the framed shot grey-box test room (content/world/camera.json)
- `features/world/defs/canyon_spec.gd`: The sunken street (al-Saila) under the area: two walls from bottom_y up to top_y between x0 and x1 (the street's width) over the area's z range z0..z1, continued extend metres beyond both ends up to ext_top_y only, with a stone base of base_height under a brick upper wall and a thin water channel down the middle
- `features/world/defs/explore_rules_def.gd`: Numbers for walking around an area: player speed and size, follower, camera, patrol, touch and interact ranges, collision wall height and the workshop prompt
- `features/world/defs/light_spec.gd`: One practical light: where it is, its colour, a real OmniLight (energy, range; only the nearest few are alive at once) and a fake light pool (an additive quad on the floor or a wall, radius in metres, cheap and always on)
- `features/world/defs/look_def.gd`: The HD-2D look as data: camera offset and field of view, tilt-shift depth of field, key light, ambient light, background and bloom
- `features/world/defs/mist_def.gd`: One drifting mist layer (content/world/mist.json): a flat transparent plane at a height, scrolling noise between two thresholds, faded where it meets geometry, near the camera and at the plane's edges
- `features/world/defs/paint_def.gd`: The painted-diorama recipe of a look (the "paint" object of a look entry): the shared painted light (bands, tints, rim, min_light floor), which offline painterly bake the world textures use, the ink outline pass, the grade (a colour LUT made from split tones, vignette, canvas grain), anti-aliasing and the painted figure
- `features/world/defs/place_def.gd`: A named spot in an area (areas.json "places"): where the player stands to use it, or the patrol lane, so code finds it by id instead of by node path
- `features/world/defs/placement.gd`: Where one building or prop stands in an area: the content id (ref), an optional name for it (chests), the position (x, z on the floor; y absolute, or the floor height when absent) and a yaw in degrees
- `features/world/defs/prop_def.gd`: A rooftop prop as data (content/world/props.json): a list of simple parts (PropPart), an optional practical light it carries, an optional box that blocks walking (collide = width, height, depth, centred on the prop's base) and, for a chest, the lid's hinge (lid_hinge x, y, z) so the "lid" part group can swing open
- `features/world/defs/prop_part.gd`: One solid piece of a prop: a box (size = width, height, depth; at = centre) or a frustum (size = bottom radius, top radius, height; at = base centre), a palette letter, an optional yaw/tilt (degrees), and how it is drawn: glow (unshaded, boosted, blooms), blink (a glow that pulses), water (rippling or falling painted water), pattern (a painted tile texture instead of the letter), group (a named sub-mesh that can move, such as a chest lid)
- `features/world/defs/prop_splash.gd`: Water drops a prop throws up where its stream lands (the sabil): a small burst of additive quads, drawn from a CPUParticles3D at `at` (prop space)
- `features/world/defs/sign_spec.gd`: One neon sign: a localization key (a place name in Musnad letters only), a dark board with a glowing frame, the glow colour, a position and yaw, the text height in metres (size) and how much it flickers
- `features/world/defs/sky_def.gd`: The night sky as data (content/world/sky.json): gradient, stars, milky way, moon, two cloud layers and the megacity glow
- `features/world/defs/skyline_band.gd`: One depth band of the skyline: city blocks on a jittered grid between min_dist and max_dist metres from the play area's edge
- `features/world/defs/skyline_def.gd`: The city around the play area as data: the ground level (y of the street, far below the rooftops), the al-Saila street (a sunken street along z at saila_x), depth bands of buildings and the landmarks
- `features/world/defs/skyline_landmark.gd`: One landmark placed by data: kind, position on the ground (x east, z south; the play area is x 0..26, z 0..18 and -Z is north), facing in degrees, main size (height or length in metres), a part count, a seed and a radius kept free of ordinary city blocks
- `features/world/defs/tile_def.gd`: One kind of block: height in metres, colour (an art-bible palette letter or #hex), whether it blocks walking, an optional glow, an optional cap tile drawn on top of it (gypsum trim on a tower) and an optional surface pattern (a SurfacePainter texture painted over the colour, 4 m repeat, 32 px = 1 m), or hidden (blocks only)
- `features/world/interact/chest.gd`: A treasure chest: the prop's body and a lid that swings open on a hinge when the player interacts
- `features/world/interact/interact_spot.gd`: Something the player can press interact next to: a floating prompt (a localization key) that shows while he is within the interact radius, and a virtual _interact() that runs on the key press
- `features/world/interact/pill_spot.gd`: An interact spot whose prompt is the UI's glass pill ("[E] Verb", Ui.interaction_prompt) instead of a 3D label: the pill follows the spot through the camera and shows while the player is in range
- `features/world/interact/sabil_drink.gd`: What drinking at the sabil does to the game: the whole party is refilled (no carried vitals = full), the cleared patrols are forgotten (they return), the save point is the sabil and the game is written to a slot
- `features/world/interact/sabil_spot.gd`: The sabil fountain: interact opens the "Drink to rest?" screen
- `features/world/interact/stall_spot.gd`: The herb stall: stand at the counter and press interact to open the shop screen (Screens id &"shop")
- `features/world/interact/talk_spot.gd`: An interact spot for talking to an NPC (e.g
- `features/world/interior/camera_room.gd`: Grey-box interior test room demonstrating FramedShots and FollowCameraRig in framed indoor mode
- `features/world/interior/camera_room.tscn`: scene
- `features/world/logic/camera_limits.gd`: The exploration camera's frame rules: the camera target is the player clamped into the area's limits (x and z ranges from camera.json), so the camera never leaves the commons even when the player walks to the east roof
- `features/world/logic/facade_details.gd`: Sana'a facade parts painted with palette letters at 32 px/m: gypsum friezes (zigzag, triangles, rosettes), windows with thick white gypsum frames, the qamariya (a semicircle of coloured glass over the window) and arched wooden doors
- `features/world/logic/facade_painter.gd`: Paints one Sana'a tower-house facade at 32 px/m from a FacadeSpec: basalt stone floors at the bottom (door on the ground floor), fired-brick floors above, a gypsum frieze at the top of each brick floor, and on every brick floor windows with gypsum frames under qamariya arches
- `features/world/logic/facade_spec.gd`: What one painted facade needs: width in metres, floors (the lowest stone_floors are basalt, the rest brick), window columns, frieze style, qamariya glass letters, lit and shutter ratios, a door, floor height in pixels and the seed
- `features/world/logic/follow_cam.gd`: Close third-person follow camera logic: focus, lazy auto-yaw, a scripted orbit (never player input: owner 2026-10-23), zone easing and arm shortening
- `features/world/logic/follow_guard.gd`: Keeps the follower from sticking: it asks to be put back on the leader's trail when it is farther than the leash, or when it wanted to move but barely got closer to the target (wedged on a corner) for stuck_seconds
- `features/world/logic/framed_shots.gd`: Indoor framed shots logic: shot picking with hysteresis, clamped tracking, and input basis retention at cuts
- `features/world/logic/light_pick.gd`: Which practical lights get a real OmniLight: the nearest few to a focus point (the rest keep only their fake light pool), plus the fade and flicker maths
- `features/world/logic/masonry.gd`: Brick courses and stone slabs painted with palette letters
- `features/world/logic/patrol_safety.gd`: Where the party may stand with respect to the patrols: distance to a patrol lane (a segment, flat on the floor), the spot to stand on after a battle (the old one if it is clear, else the nearest clear cell) and the spot "Unstuck" picks (the newest remembered spot that is clear and not where the player is wedged, else the nearest safe place)
- `features/world/logic/pixel_canvas.gd`: A pixel canvas painted with palette letters, with an optional emission layer (black = no glow)
- `features/world/logic/safe_spot.gd`: Remembers where the player last stood still (the "unstuck" targets)
- `features/world/logic/skyline_layout.gd`: Where the city blocks stand: for each band a jittered grid of cells between the band's distances from the play area, minus the al-Saila corridor and the landmark clearings, thinned by the band's fill
- `features/world/logic/stall_keeper.gd`: Where a stall keeper stands, pure: at the open end of his counter (the prop's -x end in its own frame), clear of its collide box by his body radius and a gap, so his body never pokes through the counter
- `features/world/logic/surface_painter.gd`: Seamless 128x128 surface textures (4 m at 32 px/m) for the playable tiles, painted with palette letters: lime-plaster roof floor, worn plaster, white gypsum, wooden planks, stone paving (al-Saila), basalt, brick, and the dotted window texture of far silhouettes
- `features/world/logic/walk_graph.gd`: The walk graph of an area: which one-metre cells can be stood on, which can be reached from a start, which belong to a free 2 x 2 block (a corridor under 2 m has none), where the cells are traps and where a step is too high
- `features/world/look_test/look_test.gd`: HD-2D look test (the M1 rendering spike): a block diorama, a pixel-art billboard hero (CharacterVisual), tilt-shift depth of field, bloom and a low sun with shadows
- `features/world/look_test/look_test.tscn`: scene
- `features/world/painted/logic/segment_box.gd`: Pure helpers of the camera cut-away: does the line from the camera to the party cross a box (slab test), which world boxes could ever block it (instance transforms of a mesh, tall enough), how a point weighs in the tube around the line (the same maths as occlusion_dither.gdshaderinc), and the ease of the fade amount
- `features/world/painted/tests/test_occlusion.gd`: The camera cut-away: the segment-vs-box helper (hits, misses, grazing, a segment that ends inside), the tube weight (inside, soft edge, the party's own margin, the floor), the box list of tall instances, the fade easing, and a painted rooftop whose camera line is blocked by the mafraj (the cut amount rises) and clear in the open (it falls)
- `features/world/painted/tests/test_painted_world.gd`: The painted world rules: the game look (painted_b) uses the hades camera and a brighter night, the cut-away globals exist, painted glow replaces the plain glow only while a painted look is in use, neon text is never alpha-cut, the sabil and the herb stall are painted (water, five qamariya panes, splash, stall awning and herbs), the arena look is usable, and switching looks clears every cached material
- `features/world/patrol/patrol.gd`: A Concession patrol walking its lane (two floor points, a pause at each end)
- `features/world/player/bystander.gd`: A person who stands where the level puts him (the herb seller): an idle picture turned the way the place says
- `features/world/player/follower.gd`: Bilqis: trails the leader along the path he recently walked, at the follower distance, closing in with a little lag
- `features/world/player/player.gd`: Zayd: 8-way walking from the move_* actions (up = -Z), stopped by solid tiles
- `features/world/rooftop/actor_body.gd`: The collision capsule of a walking actor (Zayd, Bilqis): radius and height come from ExploreRulesDef (explore.json; builder B4 later reads them from the ModelDef instead)
- `features/world/rooftop/area_actors.gd`: The living things of an area, built from its markers and places: Zayd, Bilqis, one Patrol per patrol place, the workshop bench, the herb stall and its seller, and the sabil
- `features/world/rooftop/area_walk.gd`: The walk graph of an area built from content: a cell can be stood on when its tile is not solid and no prop's collide box (turned by its yaw, grown by the capsule radius) covers the cell centre at the height Zayd stands
- `features/world/rooftop/patrol_director.gd`: The rules for the patrols of an area: those beaten since the last sabil drink (GameState.cleared_patrols) stay gone, the one that fought goes back to its lane start after a battle, nobody can touch for touch_grace seconds after a battle, a drink or an unstuck, and a drink brings every patrol back (docs/design/economy.md section 6)
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop.gd`: The rooftop exploration scene: builds the diorama (RooftopWorld), the actors (AreaActors) and the patrol rules (PatrolDirector); battle and menu scenes use only the public API below
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop.tscn`: scene
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_camera.gd`: What the exploration camera looks at: the player clamped into the rig's limits (so it never leaves the commons), or, during dialogue, the speaker's head
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_debug.gd`: The F3 debug labels of an area: frames per second and the area name
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_safety.gd`: Where the party may be put by the game: after a battle (the old spot if it is clear of every patrol, else the nearest clear walkable cell) and by "Unstuck" (the newest remembered still spot that is clear, else the nearest `safe` place)
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_shot.gd`: Frame tool: the rooftop with Zayd put at chosen floor coordinates (and an optional free camera), for rendering pictures
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_shot.tscn`: scene
- `features/world/rooftop/rooftop_world.gd`: Builds the still world of the rooftop scene under a host node: environment, sun, the area's blocks, mist, skyline, the camera and its ExploreCamera
- `features/world/tests/test_ambush.gd`: Which side struck first: the patrol's walking direction, and last_touch_ambush() after a touch (0 nobody, 1 the patrol caught the player from behind, 2 the player caught the patrol from behind)
- `features/world/tests/test_area.gd`: Area, tile and look content: the rooftop layout is well formed and every probe of a broken layout is caught
